stem: Joseph is a 13-month-old boy who presents after choking on spilled nuts. He initially has intermittent coughing, stridor, and increased work of breathing. While waiting for the ENT registrar, his cough becomes less effective and he appears to be losing consciousness. What is the next step in management?

options.text: Back blows followed by chest thrusts if needed
Back blows followed by abdominal thrusts if needed
Immediate direct laryngoscopy with Magills forceps to remove foreign body

explanation: A child with suspected foreign body airway obstruction who becomes unresponsive should have CPR commenced immediately, with chest compressions and reassessment for a visible foreign body before attempts at ventilation. This is the appropriate next step once the child is losing consciousness.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The child is progressing from partial to near-complete airway obstruction with reduced consciousness, which changes management from choking maneuvers to resuscitation. CPR is the next step.

optionExplanations.A: Back blows and chest thrusts are used for a conscious infant with severe airway obstruction, not when the child is becoming unresponsive.
optionExplanations.B: Abdominal thrusts are not used in infants; chest thrusts are preferred for infants with severe choking.
optionExplanations.C: A surgical airway is a last resort and not the next step here.
optionExplanations.D: Direct laryngoscopy and forceps removal may be used by skilled clinicians if the object is visible, but a deteriorating, unresponsive child should first be managed with CPR.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: loss of consciousness from suspected foreign body obstruction requires immediate CPR.

Clinical scenario 2 - Joseph

Joseph, a 13 month old boy, is bought in to the emergency department after his mother found him choking and gagging in the kitchen next to a container of spilled nuts. He appears alert and has increased work of breathing with audible stridor and subcostal retractions. His colour is normal. He is coughing intermittently. His vital signs are; RR 66/min, HR 160/min, BP 88/56, Temp 37.1ºC, SaO
